heroHeadline: Trump-Xi Summit Day 1 (May 14): 'Strategic Stability' Framework + H200 AI Chip Clearance; S&P 500 Record 7,444; Nasdaq Record 26,402; Warsh Assumes Fed Chair May 15
heroSubtitle: May 14: The most consequential diplomatic day of 2026. Trump and Xi met for 2h15m at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing — White House called it 'good'; Xi declared the economic teams produced 'generally balanced and positive outcomes.' The headline deliverable: US cleared Nvidia H200 AI chip sales to 10 Chinese firms (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD.com — 75,000 units each cap) — the largest US-China tech trade concession since export controls began. A joint 'constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability' framework was agreed, intended to guide the relationship for 3+ years. Xi's Taiwan warning was the sharpest signal from the Chinese side: 'clashes and even conflicts' if Taiwan independence is mishandled. Markets surged: S&P 500 hit record 7,444.25 (+0.5%); Nasdaq hit record 26,402.34 (+1.2%); Dow edged down 0.14%. The 10Y yield held at ~4.49% — no bond market relief despite equity jubilation, as CPI 3.8% and PPI 6.0% stagflation prints remain dominant. CEO delegation: Jensen Huang (NVIDIA), Elon Musk (Tesla), Tim Cook (Apple), Kelly Ortberg (Boeing). May 15: Kevin Warsh officially becomes Federal Reserve Chair (Powell term expires) — his first FOMC is June 9-10 with inheritance: CPI 3.8%, PPI 6.0%, core PCE 3.2%, CME hike odds ~30%. Summit Day 2 deliverables pending: Iran/Hormuz cooperation, rare earth concessions, Boeing purchase commitments, formal $30B-for-$30B tariff framework. Section 122 cliff July 23 (69 days). Recession probabilities: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~35%, Polymarket no-recession 78%.
